e: Algeria severs diplomatic relations with the United Arab Emirates, citing unspecified "provocative or hostile" acts.
A 10-year-old boy is found dead in a well in Ghassoul, El Bayadh Province, bringing an end to a four-day rescue operation which drew national attention.
Multiple heatwave-caused wildfires kill 12 people and injure 54, across several provinces.
Seventeen migrants are reported dead after attempting to cross from Algeria to Spain's Balearic Islands, with two survivors.
A bus plunges into a ravine near Boumerdès, killing 28 people. President Tebboune declares three days of national mourning for the victims.
The United States imposes a 12.5% tariff on Algeria, citing the presence of alleged forced labour in the supply chain.
A fire at an orphanage in the Mohammadia district of Algiers kills 11 people and injures 19 others.
Mali restores diplomatic relations with Algeria after a yearlong rift.
China lifts tariffs on imports from Algeria until 2028.
A boat carrying migrants from Somalia capsizes off Bou Ismaïl, killing 17 passengers.
Former industry minister Ali Aoun is sentenced to five years' imprisonment for corruption by a court in Algiers over the irregular sale of ferrous and non-ferrous metal waste.
Pope Leo XIV arrives in Algiers for a two-day visit, becoming the first pontiff to visit Algeria.
Two bombers die in a suicide attack near a police station in Blida.
Seven militants are killed by the Algerian Army during two counter-terrorism operations in Tebessa Province; three soldiers are also killed in the clashes.
Two people are killed and four others are injured when a Beechcraft 1900 of the Algerian Air Force crashes at Boufarik Airport near Boufarik, Blida Province.
At least six people are killed and 15 others are injured when a passenger bus and a semi-trailer truck collide in Tamacine, Touggourt Province.
President Tebboune dismisses Bank of Algeria governor Salah Eddine Taleb by presidential decree, and appoints deputy governor Mouatassem Boudiaf as acting governor.
